title: Past and future
goal: Say what you did and what you will do, give reasons, say "if" and "can't", and suggest doing things together.

notes.p: Look at the last vowel of the stem. If it is ㅏ or ㅗ, add {{았어요}}; otherwise add {{었어요}}; {{하다}} becomes {{했어요}}. Vowels often merge: {{가다}} becomes {{갔어요}}, {{오다}} becomes {{왔어요}}, {{보다}} becomes {{봤어요}}, {{마시다}} becomes {{마셨어요}}. Korean also uses the past for "I'm late" ({{늦었어요}}): the being-late has already happened. Sound point: the ㅆ carries over to the next vowel, so {{갔어요}} sounds like "ga-sseo-yo".
ex: What did you do on the weekend?

notes.p: After a vowel, add ㄹ and {{거예요}}: {{가다}} becomes {{갈 거예요}}. After a consonant, add {{을 거예요}}: {{먹을 거예요}}. Words ending in ㅂ change again: {{덥다}} becomes {{더울 거예요}}. Spelling trap: it is always written {{거예요}} with ㅖ, even though many Koreans misspell it with ㅔ. Sound point: {{거}} is said with a tight k, so {{갈 거예요}} sounds like "gal kkeo-ye-yo".
ex: What are you going to do tomorrow?
I'm going to eat Korean food.

notes.p: {{아서}} / {{어서}} ({{해서}} for {{하다}} words) joins a reason to its result: {{바빠서 못 가요}}, "I'm busy, so I can't go". The reason part never takes its own past ending; the last verb shows the time: {{어제 바빠서 못 갔어요}}. Koreans don't use it before "let's" or "shall we". {{면}} after a vowel and {{으면}} after a consonant means "if": {{비가 오면}}, {{시간 있으면}}.
ex: I'm tired, so I want to go home.
I was busy yesterday, so I couldn't go.
If you have time, let's eat together.

notes.p: {{안}} means you don't or won't, by choice. {{못}} means you can't, even if you'd like to. Both go right before the verb: {{못 가요}}. {{잘 못해요}} means "I'm not good at it". Sound point: {{못}} changes the sound after it. {{못 가요}} sounds like "mot kka-yo", {{못해요}} like "mo-tae-yo", and {{못 먹어요}} like "mon meo-geo-yo".
ex: I'm busy, so I can't go.
My Korean isn't very good yet.

notes.h: Ever, shall we, go to: three handy patterns
notes.p: "Have you ever …?": take the {{아요}} / {{어요}} form, drop {{요}}, and add {{본 적 있어요?}}: {{가요}} gives {{가 본 적 있어요?}} Answer {{네, 있어요}} or {{아니요, 없어요}}. "Shall we …?": {{ㄹ까요?}} after a vowel, {{을까요?}} after a consonant: {{갈까요?}}, {{먹을까요?}} Going somewhere to do something: stem + {{러}} (or {{으러}} after a consonant) + {{가요}}: {{영화 보러 가요}}, {{밥 먹으러 가요}}.
ex: Have you ever been to Korea?
Shall we go see a movie?

items.en: I met a friend yesterday.
items.why: {{어제}} needs the past. {{만나}} ends in ㅏ, so it takes {{았어요}}, and the vowels merge: {{만났어요}}.

items.en: I drank coffee yesterday.
items.why: {{마시}} + {{었어요}} merges into {{마셨어요}}. The past always ends in {{어요}}, so {{마셨요}} is missing a syllable.

items.en: I watched a movie on the weekend.
items.why: {{보}} ends in ㅗ, so it takes {{았어요}}: {{봤어요}}.

items.en: I'm going to eat Korean food tomorrow.
items.why: After a consonant, {{을 거예요}}. It is always spelled {{거예요}}, never with ㅔ.

items.en: I'll go tomorrow.
items.why: {{가}} ends in a vowel, so just add ㄹ: {{갈 거예요}}.

items.en: I'm busy, so I can't go.
items.why: {{아서}} = so / because, and {{바쁘다}} drops its ㅡ: {{바빠서}}. {{바쁘면}} would mean "if I'm busy".

items.en: If you have time, let's watch a movie together.
items.why: After a consonant, {{으면}}: {{있으면}}. {{어서}} can't lead into "let's".

items.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
items.why: {{오}} ends in a vowel, so just {{면}}: {{오면}}. {{와서}} would mean "because it's raining".

items.en: I can't eat pork.
items.why: {{못}} = can't. {{안 먹어요}} would mean you don't eat it by choice.

items.en: Have you ever tried Korean food?
items.why: The pattern is fixed: {{본 적 있어요?}}

items.en: Have you ever seen a Korean movie?
items.why: Take the {{요}} off {{봐요}} and add {{본 적 있어요}}: {{봐 본 적 있어요?}}

items.en: Shall we have dinner together?
items.why: {{먹}} ends in a consonant, so it takes {{을까요}}: {{먹을까요?}}

items.en: I'm going to see a movie on the weekend.
items.why: Stem + {{러}} + {{가요}} = go to do something: {{보러 가요}}.

items.en: What did you do yesterday?
items.why: {{하다}} becomes {{했어요}} in the past.

items.en: I haven't eaten yet.
items.why: "Haven't … yet" is {{아직 안}} + past: {{아직 안 먹었어요}}.

items.en: It will be hot tomorrow.
items.why: ㅂ words change before a vowel: {{덥}} + {{을}} becomes {{더울}}.

items.q: A friend asks {{밥 먹었어요?}} You haven't eaten yet. You say:
items.why: {{아직이요}} = not yet.

items.q: You arrive ten minutes after the time you agreed to meet. You say:
items.why: Once you are already late, Korean uses the past: {{늦었어요}}. {{늦을 거예요}} is for warning someone ahead of time.

items.q: A coworker praises your Korean. You answer modestly:
items.why: {{잘 못해요}} = I'm not good at it. {{잘 안 해요}} would mean you don't often speak it.

items.q: You want to suggest getting together and let your friend choose the time. You ask:
items.why: {{ㄹ까요?}} = shall we …? {{만났어요?}} asks about the past, and {{몇 시예요?}} asks the time now.

items.q: You've never been to Korea. Someone asks {{한국에 가 본 적 있어요?}} You say:
items.why: Answer a {{본 적 있어요?}} question with {{있어요}} or {{없어요}}.

items.q: A friend invites you out tonight, but you're too tired. You say:
items.why: {{해서}} gives the reason and {{못 가요}} says you can't go. {{피곤하면}} means "if I'm tired", and {{못 갔어요}} is past.

items.q: Dinner at a friend's home is over. You tell the host the food was great:
items.why: The meal is over, so use the past: {{맛있었어요}}. {{맛있게 드세요}} = enjoy your meal.

items.q: A friend asks where you're heading. You're going out to get coffee. You say:
items.why: Stem + {{러}} + {{가요}} = going (somewhere) to do something.

I'm going to watch a movie tomorrow.

I've never been to Korea.

Shall we go eat together?
I'm tired, so I'm going home.
I watched a movie with friends.
I'm going to Korea to learn Korean.
Yesterday was really fun.

turns.en: What did you do on the weekend?

turns.why: She asks about the past, so answer in the past: {{봤어요}}.
{{아직이요}} = not yet. {{아직}} with a plain past doesn't make sense, and {{네}} + future doesn't answer "have you eaten?".
{{같이 가요}} = let's go together. {{갔어요}} is past.

turns.en: What do you want to eat?

turns.why: You're already late, so Korean uses the past: {{늦었어요}}.

turns.s: 괜찮아요. 저도 방금 도착했어요. 뭐 마실래요?
turns.en: That's okay. I just got here too. What would you like to drink?

turns.why: {{ㄹ래요}} = I'll have. {{마셨어요}} is past, and {{러}} needs {{가요}} after it.

turns.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?

turns.why: He asks about tomorrow, so use the future: {{만날 거예요}}.

turns.en: Do you have time on Sunday?
Shall we go see a Korean movie?

turns.why: Suggest a plan with {{만날까요?}}; {{만났어요?}} asks about the past.

turns.en: Have you ever been to Korea?
Do you want to go to Korea?

turns.why: Answer {{가고 싶어요?}} with {{가고 싶어요}}. You just said you have never been.

turns.en: If you go to Korea, what will you do?

turns.why: She asks about the future, so {{먹을 거예요}}.

roleplay.title: Monday catch-up
roleplay.setup: It's Monday morning. A Korean friend asks about your weekend. Tell her what you did and ask about hers.
roleplay.persona: You are Minji, a friendly Korean friend in Chicago. On the weekend you went to a Korean restaurant with friends on Saturday and stayed home on Sunday because it rained. Speak simple polite Korean (해요 style) using mostly words from levels 1-6: past -았/었어요, future -(으)ㄹ 거예요, -아서/어서, 못. Ask follow-up questions like 재미있었어요? and 뭐 먹었어요? Keep sentences short and never use casual speech.
roleplay.opening_en: What did you do on the weekend?
goals: Say two things you did on the weekend
Say what you will do this evening

roleplay.title: Making a plan
roleplay.setup: A Korean friend wants to see a movie with you tomorrow. Accept, or say you can't and why, then agree on a time.
roleplay.persona: You are Junho, a Korean friend. You want to see a Korean movie tomorrow evening; showings are at six and eight o'clock. If the learner can't come, suggest another day. Speak simple polite Korean (해요 style) using mostly words from levels 1-6, including -(으)ㄹ까요?, -(으)러 가요, -(으)면 and 못. Keep sentences short.
roleplay.opening: 내일 시간 있어요? 같이 영화 보러 갈까요?
roleplay.opening_en: Are you free tomorrow? Shall we go see a movie together?
goals: Accept, or say you can't and give a reason with -aseo / -eoseo
Say what else you will do tomorrow with -(eu)l geoyeyo
Ask if he has ever been to Korea
